deities: Lord Vishnu as Ananthapadmanabha (seated on the serpent Anantha, flanked by Sridevi and Bhudevi)

history.summary: Hindu Vishnu temple at Ananthapura, ~6 km from Kumbla in Manjeshwaram taluk - the only lake temple in Kerala, with the sanctum standing on a small island reached by a single foot-bridge. Tradition holds it is the moolasthanam (original abode) of Ananthapadmanabhaswamy of the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Thiruvananthapuram: the sage Vilvamangalthu Swami is said to have followed the deity through a cave at the lake's corner southwards. The temple has no flagstaff; its annual festival centres on the balikkal (sacrificial stone). The main idol is a rare seated (not reclining) Ananthapadmanabha flanked by Sridevi and Bhudevi. The lake was long home to Babiya, a vegetarian crocodile revered as the temple's guardian and messenger, fed on prasadam of rice and jaggery; Babiya died on 9 October 2022. The idols are said to be made by the Kadusharkara yogam process from about 108 materials.

name: Ananthapura Lake Temple
town_description: Ananthapura is a small village in Manjeshwaram taluk of Kasaragod district, about 6 km from Kumbla town on the Kasaragod-Mangalore National Highway 66. It is an agrarian settlement in the Tulu-Kannada-Malayalam cultural belt of north Kerala. The village is best known for the lake temple at its centre, revered as the moolasthanam (original abode) of the famous Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple at Thiruvananthapuram.

travel.road: On NH 66; ~6 km from Kumbla, ~12 km from Kasaragod town; autos and buses available

visitor_information.best_time: September-March; April for the Teppotsavam float festival
